organization: Illinois General Assembly (225 ILCS 515/1.1 via FindLaw statute mirror)
title: Private Employment Agency Act, Sec. 1.1 Definitions
claim: 'Employment agency' excludes any person in the business of consulting or recruiting compensated solely by an employer to identify, appraise or recommend individuals (>=18 or HS diploma) for a position, provided the individual is never charged a fee directly or indirectly, including for resume preparation or any other personal service; exclusion not applicable to theatrical or domestic service agencies. 'Employment counselor' includes an employee who solicits orders from employers.
excerpt: 'does not include any person engaged in the business of consulting or recruiting ... compensated solely by any employer'
limitations: Mirror text 'current as of January 01, 2025'; ilga.gov returned HTTP 503 on 2026-11-28 so the official site could not be checked.

title: Private Employment Agency FAQ (re-accessed)
claim: FAQ 1 repeats the consulting/recruiting exclusion for firms compensated solely by an employer (not for theatrical/domestic agencies); FAQ 7: Department may refuse/suspend/revoke licences and the Act carries criminal sanctions; FAQ 14: each location needs a separate licence and bond; FAQ 19: licensed agencies may not take an applicant fee until the applicant accepts a position.
excerpt: 'excluding any person engaged in the business of consulting or recruiting' ... 'compensated solely by any employer'
limitations: Agency FAQ paraphrasing the statute; does not address remote/out-of-state operation.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (820 ILCS 112/10 via FindLaw mirror)
title: Illinois Equal Pay Act of 2003, Sec. 10
claim: (b-5) unlawful for an employer OR EMPLOYMENT AGENCY to screen applicants on wage/salary history or require salary history; (b-25) employers with 15+ employees must include pay scale and benefits in postings; if an employer engages a third party to post, the third party must include them and is liable for omission unless the employer did not provide the information; an employer or employment agency must disclose pay scale and benefits to an applicant on request before an offer; asking pay expectations is allowed.
excerpt: 'The third party is liable for failure to include the pay scale and benefits in the job posting'
limitations: Mirror current as of 2025-01-01; (b-25) applies to postings after the effective date of the 103rd GA amendatory Act (understood to be 2025-01-01; confirm).

organization: Illinois General Assembly (820 ILCS 75/15 via FindLaw mirror)
title: Job Opportunities for Qualified Applicants Act, Sec. 15
claim: An employer or employment agency may not inquire about, consider or require disclosure of an applicant's criminal record until the applicant is determined qualified and selected for an interview, or, if no interview, after a conditional offer.
excerpt: 'An employer or employment agency may not inquire about or into, consider, or require disclosure of the criminal record'
limitations: Mirror current as of 2025-01-01.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (820 ILCS 42/5 via FindLaw mirror)
title: Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act, Sec. 5
claim: An employer that asks applicants to record video interviews and uses AI analysis must notify each applicant, explain how the AI works and what it evaluates, and obtain consent before the interview; may not use AI to evaluate non-consenting applicants.
excerpt: 'Obtain, before the interview, consent from the applicant to be evaluated by the artificial intelligence program'
limitations: Text addresses 'employer'; coverage of third-party recruiters not stated.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (820 ILCS 90/10 via FindLaw mirror)
title: Illinois Freedom to Work Act, Sec. 10
claim: Non-competes void unless the employee's actual or expected annualized earnings exceed $75,000 ($80,000 from 2027-01-01); non-solicits void unless earnings exceed $45,000 ($47,500 from 2027-01-01).
excerpt: 'increase to $80,000 per year beginning on January 1, 2027'
limitations: Mirror text; other conditions (adequate consideration, legitimate business interest, 14-day review) not captured.

title: Illinois Takes Aim at Artificial Intelligence in Employment
claim: HB 3773 (Public Act 103-0804) amends the Illinois Human Rights Act effective 2026-01-01: civil-rights violation to use AI with discriminatory effect in recruitment, hiring, promotion, discipline etc.; zip codes may not be used as a proxy for protected classes; employers must notify when AI is used; IDHR to adopt rules.
excerpt: Protects against 'discriminatory AI practices' (paraphrase of law-firm summary)
limitations: Law-firm summary; ilga.gov Public Act page unavailable (503); does not address employment agencies explicitly.

organization: Seyfarth Shaw / Baker McKenzie (via web-search summary)
title: IDHR temporarily withdraws proposed rules on use of AI in employment
claim: IDHR proposed Subpart J (56 Ill. Adm. Code 2520.900 et seq.) on AI in employment in May 2026 (comments to 2026-06-29) and withdrew it on 2026-06-02, cancelling the 2026-06-10 hearing; status after June 2026 unconfirmed.
excerpt: Search summary: withdrawal described as temporary.
limitations: Seen only through search-result summaries (pages returned 403/404); re-check the Illinois Register.

title: Robert Half Annual Report FY2023, MD&A
claim: Permanent placement revenues $567M in 2023 vs $725M in 2022 (-21.7%), driven by a 24.1% decrease in placements partly offset by a 2.4% increase in average fees; combined segment income 13.2% of revenue (2023) vs 17.6% (2022); perm gross margin 99.8%.
excerpt: 'a 24.1% decrease in the number of placements'
limitations: Incumbent economics; national scale, mostly finance/accounting and admin roles.

title: Robert Half Annual Report FY2025, MD&A and Item 1
claim: Perm revenue $440M in 2025 vs $487M in 2024 (-9.8%): placements -13.6%, average fees +3.8%; perm segment operating margin 2.9% vs 7.7%; SG&A 96.9% of perm revenue; perm demand 'even more sensitive to economic and labor market conditions' than contract; ~14,500 full-time internal staff incl. ~7,100 Protiviti; AI risk factor.
excerpt: 'demand for permanent placement talent solutions is even more sensitive to economic and labor market conditions'
limitations: Incumbent; recruiter headcount not disclosed.

title: Robert Half Annual Report FY2009, MD&A
claim: Permanent placement revenues $182M in 2009, down 57% (56% constant currency) from $427M in 2008, which was down 4% from $444M in 2007.
excerpt: 'Permanent placement revenues were $182 million for the year ended December 31, 2009, down 57%'
limitations: Incumbent; finance/accounting-heavy mix; the Great Recession is the severe-case analogue.

title: Kforce Annual Report FY2025
claim: Direct Hire revenue $25.7M (2025, -11.1%), $28.9M (2024, -24.0%), $38.0M (2023); recorded net of a fallout reserve, contingency period typically 90 days or less; recognised when candidate has accepted, resigned and starts within the following month; MSPs/VMOs/VMS providers charge staffing firms 1-4% of revenue and have caused gross-margin compression; AI listed as a competitive risk.
excerpt: 'Direct Hire revenue is recorded net of a fallout reserve.'
limitations: Incumbent with national/MSP-heavy clients; fallout rate itself not disclosed.

title: Full year results for the year ended 31 December 2025 (preliminary)
claim: Gross profit GBP769.5m (-7.6% cc); permanent 72% of GP; GP per fee earner GBP148.9k (2024 GBP150.0k); fee earners 4,968 (-402, -7.5%), cut mostly via natural attrition; conversion (EBIT/GP) 2.7% (2024 6.2%); Americas conversion 3.2%; North America GP +8%, US +9% with strong Manufacturing; interview-to-offer conversion the biggest challenge, extending time-to-hire; AI expected to remain a supporting tool for consultants, not a replacement.
excerpt: 'Gross profit per fee earner, our measure of productivity, remains high'
limitations: Incumbent, global, mostly white-collar; GBP figures (~$195k per fee earner at ~$1.31/GBP is an analyst conversion); preliminary (unaudited) results.
